they found Mr. Racette had a loaded sawed-off shotgun in a backpack under his vest
rationale_highlights: Mr. Racette's maternal grandmother was aboriginal and may have attended a residential school.
His childhood was marked by poverty, family violence and substance abuse, disconnection from his aboriginal community
He experienced bullying and racism throughout his school years

I accept that Mr. Racette's commission of the first dial-a-dope offence is related to his drug addiction and efforts to fuel it, which in turn is connected to his background, aboriginal heritage and all that entails.
I further accept that these factors significantly reduce his moral blameworthiness.

Were it not for these factors, given his extensive criminal record and the fact he was bound by a recognizance at the time, in my view it is likely a sentence well above the bottom of the usual range would be appropriate.
note: Appeal court's own finding at para 22; applies to trafficking count
